title: Rava bar Sheva
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman calls him Ravina’s student. In the account at [Shabbat 140a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.140a.6) (cited by Hyman as 139b), he says, “I was standing before Ravina. It was stirred for him with a garlic stalk, and he ate it.”[^1]

In [Berakhot 14a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.14a.5-6), Rav [Rava, according to Dikdukei Soferim] bar Sheva came to Ravina on a day when an individual does not recite the complete Hallel. Ravina did not interrupt for him, because Ravina did not regard Rava bar Sheva as sufficiently important.[^2]
Hyman says Seder HaDorot conflated him with Rav bar Sheva, who was a student of Rav Nachman.[^3]

notes.text: Hyman’s [printed article (vol. III, p. 1061)](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/ba/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._III._1910.pdf#page=228) gives Shabbat 139b and reads ליה, “for him,” as does Shabbat 140a. The supplied Hebrew transcription instead has לי, “for me.”

Berakhot reads Rav bar Sheva. [Dikdukei Soferim](https://www.google.com/books/edition/_/ZWuq1txyjt8C?hl=en&gbpv=1&pg=RA1-PA62) records a manuscript reading with Rava and an additional Rav before Sheva.

[Heilprin’s Rav bar Sheva entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3073&lang=en) assigns him the Shabbat episode. [The Rava bar Sheva heading](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3126&lang=en) refers readers to the Rav entry. Hyman disputes that identification.
